{{Short description|Topological soliton}}{{Confusing|date=November 2024}}[[File:Hopfion.png|thumb|Model of magnetic hopfion in a solid. B<sub>em</sub> is emergent magnetic field (orange arrows); in a hopfion, it does not align to the external magnetic field (black arrow).]]
A '''hopfion''' is a [[topological defect|topological soliton]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal | vauthors = Faddeev L, Niemi AJ |title=Stable knot-like structures in classical field theory |journal=Nature |date= 1997 |volume=387 |issue=6628 |pages=58–61 |doi=10.1038/387058a0|arxiv=hep-th/9610193 |bibcode=1997Natur.387...58F |s2cid=4256682 }}
</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book| vauthors = Manton N, Sutcliffe P |title=Topological solitons |date=2004 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=0-511-21141-4 |location=Cambridge |oclc=144618426 |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511617034}}
</ref><ref name="kent">{{cite journal | vauthors = Kent N, Reynolds N, Raftrey D, Campbell IT, Virasawmy S, Dhuey S, Chopdekar RV, Hierro-Rodriguez A, Sorrentino A, Pereiro E, Ferrer S, Hellman F, Sutcliffe P, Fischer P | display-authors = 6 | title = Creation and observation of Hopfions in magnetic multilayer systems | journal = Nature Communications | volume = 12 | issue = 1 | page = 1562 | date = March 2021 | pmid = 33692363 | pmc = 7946913 | doi = 10.1038/s41467-021-21846-5 | arxiv = 2010.08674 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 2021NatCo..12.1562K }}</ref> It is a stable three-dimensional localised configuration of a three-component field <math>\vec{n}=(n_x,n_y,n_z)</math> of unit length with a knotted topological structure. They are the three-dimensional counterparts of 2D [[skyrmions]], which exhibit similar topological properties in 2D. Hopfions are widely studied in many physical systems over the last half century.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hopfions in modern physics. Hopfion description |url=http://hopfion.com |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=hopfion.com}}</ref> 

The soliton is mobile and stable: i.e. it is protected from a decay by an [[activation energy|energy barrier]]. It can be deformed but always conserves an integer Hopf topological invariant. It is named after the German mathematician, [[Heinz Hopf]].

A model that supports hopfions was proposed as follows:<ref name=":0" />

<math>H= (\partial {\bf n})^2 + (\epsilon_{ijk}{\bf n}\cdot\partial_i {\bf n}\times \partial_j{\bf n})^2</math>

The terms of higher-order derivatives are required to stabilize the hopfions.

Stable hopfions were predicted within various physical platforms, including Yang–Mills theory,<ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Faddeev L, Niemi AJ |date=1999|title=Partially Dual Variables in SU(2) Yang-Mills Theory|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=82|issue=8|pages=1624–1627|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.1624|arxiv=hep-th/9807069|bibcode=1999PhRvL..82.1624F|s2cid=8281134}}</ref> superconductivity<ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors =- Babaev E, Faddeev LD, Niemi AJ |date=2002|title=Hidden symmetry and knot solitons in a charged two-condensate Bose system|journal=Physical Review B|volume=65|issue=10|article-number=100512|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.65.100512|arxiv=cond-mat/0106152|bibcode=2002PhRvB..65j0512B|s2cid=118910995}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Rybakov FN, Garaud J, Babaev E |date=2019|title=Stable Hopf-Skyrme topological excitations in the superconducting state|journal=Physical Review B|volume=100|issue=9|article-number=094515|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.100.094515|arxiv=1807.02509|bibcode=2019PhRvB.100i4515R|s2cid=118991170}}</ref> and magnetism.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Sutcliffe P | title = Skyrmion Knots in Frustrated Magnets | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 118 | issue = 24 | article-number = 247203 | date = June 2017 | pmid = 28665663 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.247203 | arxiv = 1705.10966 | s2cid = 29890978 | bibcode = 2017PhRvL.118x7203S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal| vauthors = Rybakov FN, Kiselev NS, Borisov AB, Döring L, Melcher C, Blügel S |date=2022|title=Magnetic hopfions in solids|journal=APL Materials |volume=10 |issue=11 |doi=10.1063/5.0099942 |arxiv=1904.00250|bibcode=2022APLM...10k1113R }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Tai JB, Smalyukh II | title = Static Hopf solitons and knotted emergent fields in solid-state noncentrosymmetric magnetic nanostructures | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 121  | article-number = 187201 | date = 2018 | pmid = 30444399 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.187201 | s2cid = 216036015 | bibcode = 2020PhRvL.125e7201V | arxiv = 1806.00453 }}</ref><ref name="kent" />

== Experimental observation ==
Hopfions have been observed experimentally in chiral colloidal magnetic materials,<ref name=":1">{{cite journal | vauthors = Ackerman PJ, Smalyukh II |title=Static three-dimensional topological solitons in fluid chiral ferromagnets and colloids|journal= Nature Materials|date= 2017 |volume= 16 |issue=4 |pages=426–432 |doi=10.1038/nmat4826 |pmid=27992419 |bibcode=2017NatMa..16..426A |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat4826|url-access=subscription }}
</ref> in chiral liquid crystals,<ref name=":AckermanSmalyukh">{{cite journal | vauthors = Ackerman PJ, Smalyukh II |title=Diversity of knot solitons in liquid crystals manifested by linking of preimages in torons and hopfions|journal= Physical Review X|date= 2017 |volume= 7 |issue=1 |article-number=011006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.7.011006 |arxiv=1704.08196 |bibcode=2017PhRvX...7a1006A |url=https://journals.aps.org/prx/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevX.7.011006}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-08 |title=The Spintronics Technology Revolution Could Be Just a Hopfion Away |url=https://newscenter.lbl.gov/2021/04/08/spintronics-tech-a-hopfion-away/ |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Berkeley Lab News Center |language=en-US}}</ref> in Ir/Co/Pt multilayers using [[X-ray magnetic circular dichroism]]<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Kent N, Reynolds N, Raftrey D, Campbell IT, Virasawmy S, Dhuey S, Chopdekar RV, Hierro-Rodriguez A, Sorrentino A, Pereiro E, Ferrer S, Hellman F, Sutcliffe P, Fischer P | display-authors = 6 | title = Creation and observation of Hopfions in magnetic multilayer systems | journal = Nature Communications | volume = 12 | issue = 1 | page = 1562 | date = March 2021 | pmid = 33692363 | pmc = 7946913 | doi = 10.1038/s41467-021-21846-5 | arxiv = 2010.08674 | bibcode = 2021NatCo..12.1562K | doi-access = free }}</ref> and in the polarization of free-space monochromatic light.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Sugic D, Droop R, Otte E, Ehrmanntraut D, Nori F, Ruostekoski J, Denz C, Dennis MR | display-authors = 6 | title = Particle-like topologies in light | journal = Nature Communications | volume = 12 | issue = 1 | page = 6785 | date = November 2021 | pmid = 34811373 | pmc = 8608860 | doi = 10.1038/s41467-021-26171-5  | doi-access = free| arxiv = 2107.10810 | bibcode = 2021NatCo..12.6785S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ehrmanntraut |first1=Daniel |last2=Droop |first2=Ramon |last3=Sugic |first3=Danica |last4=Otte |first4=Eileen |last5=Dennis |first5=Mark |last6=Denz |first6=Cornelia |author-link6=Cornelia Denz |date=June 2023 |title=Optical second-order skyrmionic hopfion |journal=Optica |volume=10 |issue=6 |pages=725–731 |doi=10.1364/OPTICA.487989 |bibcode=2023Optic..10..725E |via=Optica publishing group|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In chiral magnets, a helical-background variant of the hopfion has been theoretically predicted to occur within the spiral magnetic phase, where it was called a "heliknoton".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Voinescu |first1=Robert |last2=Tai |first2=Jung-Shen B. |last3=Smalyukh |first3=Ivan I. |title=Hopf Solitons in Helical and Conical Backgrounds of Chiral Magnetic Solids |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=27 July 2020 |volume=125 |issue=5 |article-number=057201 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.057201 |pmid=32794865 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.057201|arxiv=2004.10109 |bibcode=2020PhRvL.125e7201V }}</ref> In recent years, the concept of a "fractional hopfion" has also emerged where not all preimages of magnetisation have a nonzero linking.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yu |first1=Xiuzhen |last2=Liu |first2=Yizhou |last3=Iakoubovskii |first3=Konstantin V. |last4=Nakajima |first4=Kiyomi |last5=Kanazawa |first5=Naoya |last6=Nagaosa |first6=Naoto |last7=Tokura |first7=Yoshinori |title=Realization and Current-Driven Dynamics of Fractional Hopfions and Their Ensembles in a Helimagnet FeGe |journal=Advanced Materials |date=May 2023 |volume=35 |issue=20 |doi=10.1002/adma.202210646 |language=en |issn=0935-9648|doi-access=free |bibcode=2023AdM....3510646Y }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Azhar |first1=Maria |last2=Kravchuk |first2=Volodymyr P. |last3=Garst |first3=Markus |title=Screw Dislocations in Chiral Magnets |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=12 April 2022 |volume=128 |issue=15 |article-number=157204 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.157204 |pmid=35499887 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.157204|arxiv=2109.04338 |bibcode=2022PhRvL.128o7204A }}</ref>
